relevance_note: Single case report of a girl with a TNFAIP3 variant: "The analysis identified a likely pathogenic variant in TNFAIP3".
method_note: Read by hand; rows written via a short Python script in scratch and every span checked verbatim against the paper. One in-scope person (the single unnamed case-report patient, label 'patient'). Parents are mentioned (reported symptoms; planned but delayed Sanger testing) but are neither tested nor described as affected, so no rows. The literature-review part gives only cohort-level counts (e.g. systematic review of 177 cases) and no individual-level facts about other people, so no further rows. No variant rows for PIK3R1, HBB, SERPINA1 or the VPS37A VUS: genes named without a printed variant. MEFV testing negative is a genetic test, not recorded as a phenotype. Onset: abstract says 'from age 2' while the case text says 'from the age of second year' (could mean during the second year); used the abstract's 'from age 2' (P2Y). Age at last evaluation recorded as the age at report/presentation ('5-year-old'); an eight-month infliximab follow-up followed, with no age given. Pathogenicity wording varies within the paper: 'likely pathogenic' (abstract, case presentation), 'pathogenic variant' (introduction) and 'probable pathogenic variants' (discussion); recorded 'likely pathogenic'. Zygosity, variant type and inheritance not stated for this patient (only general statements about HA20 being heterozygous loss-of-function), so 'not reported'. Checklist judgements: eye redness/pain and eyelid swelling recorded as features but 'uveitis or other ocular inflammation' left not reported, since ocular inflammation is not stated and the ophthalmologic investigation was negative. GI symptoms (abdominal pain, diarrhea, perianal swelling) recorded, but 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation' left not reported because GI investigation (imaging, stool calprotectin) was negative and IBD findings absent; the authors only speculate perianal involvement 'may represent an extension of gastrointestinal mucosal inflammation'. The infantile febrile seizure is recorded as a feature, but 'central nervous system involvement' left not reported because the authors call it possibly 'comorbid or coincidental'. ANA negative recorded as excluded 'positive ANA' but the composite checklist item 'autoantibodies (ANA/other)' left not reported (narrower absence). 'CRP Weakly Positive' (Table 1) taken as observed elevated inflammatory markers; ESR 14 mm/hr and other numeric labs (e.g. hemoglobin 10.6 g/dL) are given without interpretation and were not turned into features. Negative ophthalmologic and gastrointestinal investigations recorded as the paper words them (whole investigations), excluding nothing more specific.
